title: Who Is Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
subtitle: The life, message, and human example of Islam's final prophet
summary: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca around 570 CE, began receiving revelation around 610, migrated to Medina in 622, and died in 632. Muslims believe he was God's servant and final messenger: deeply loved and followed, but never divine or worshipped.

sections.title: Understanding Who Is Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
sections.body: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca around 570 CE, received revelation around 610, migrated to Medina in 622, and died in 632. Muslims believe he was God's servant and final messenger, never divine.

sections.title: From Mecca to the First Revelation
sections.body: Muhammad was born among Quraysh and was known as al-Amin, the trustworthy. He worked in trade and married Khadijah, his first believer and steadfast supporter. Around 610, Gabriel brought the first revelation near Mecca. The message called to Tawhid, resurrection, repentance, justice, and care for the weak. Early Muslims faced persecution; some found safety in Christian Aksum.

sections.title: The Hijrah and the Medinan Community
sections.body: In 622, Muhammad and his followers migrated to Medina. He joined emigrants with local supporters, built the mosque, made agreements, taught social duties, and led through diplomacy and conflict. Badr (624) was a Muslim victory; Uhud (625) brought losses; the Trench (627) stopped a siege. Hudaybiyyah (628) created a truce. After allies were attacked, Muhammad entered Mecca in 630 with limited fighting and a widely reported amnesty. He died in Medina in 632.

sections.title: His Marriages and Family Life
sections.body: Muhammad was married only to Khadijah for about twenty-five years. Later marriages included widows, divorcees, and women from other tribes. Early Muslim accounts describe companionship, care, reconciliation, and family bonds. Some reports remain debated. The Quran calls his wives Mothers of the Believers (Quran 33:6). Umm Salamah advised him at Hudaybiyyah, and Aisha became a major teacher. Sahih Muslim 2328a reports that he never struck a woman or servant; Quran 4:19 commands kindness to wives.

sections.title: Difficult Episodes and Responsible Reading
sections.body: A credible biography should not hide difficult reports. Muhammad led campaigns amid tribal alliances, persecution, treaties, and war. Reports about Banu Qurayza require attention to dates, transmission, context, and later reconstruction. Scholars and historians disagree on details. The same care applies to reports about Aisha's marriage and seventh-century social setting. Honest history can address hard questions while recognizing Muhammad's worship, mercy, law, family life, diplomacy, and moral teaching.

sections.title: A Messenger, Not a Divine Being
sections.body: The Quran places Muhammad among human messengers and calls him the seal of the prophets (Quran 33:40). Quran 3:144 reminds believers that messengers died before him. Islam therefore loves and follows Muhammad without worshipping him. His message is universal, and the Quran is the final scripture.

sections.title: Why His Example Matters
sections.body: The Sunnah is Muhammad's example in worship, judgment, family life, business, mercy, and justice. Hadith reports vary in strength, so scholars assess transmitters and texts. Following him means learning the religious purpose of his character: sincerity, truthfulness, patience, courage, generosity, consultation, and justice. Admiration should rest on knowledge and lead back to the God he worshipped.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Who Is Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
sections.body: Muhammad ﷺ received revelation in Mecca, formed a community in Medina, and died in 632. His life joined Tawhid, worship, mercy, justice, family responsibility, diplomacy, and public leadership. Muslims honor him as God's final messenger, never as divine.

quranVerses.arabic: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ ۚ أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبْ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًۭٔا ۗ وَسَيَجْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
quranVerses.translation: Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلنَّبِىُّ أَوْلَىٰ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ ۖ وَأَزْوَٰجُهُۥٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمْ ۗ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍۢ فِى كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفْعَلُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِكُم مَّعْرُوفًۭا ۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَسْطُورًۭا
quranVerses.translation: The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are [in the position of] their mothers. And those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you may do to your close associates a kindness [through bequest]. That was in the Book inscribed.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُوا۟ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهًۭا ۖ وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا۟ بِبَعْضِ مَآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٍۢ مُّبَيِّنَةٍۢ ۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ فَإِن كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيْـًۭٔا وَيَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًۭا كَثِيرًۭا
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍۢ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمًۭا
quranVerses.translation: Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and last of the prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

faq.question: What does the symbol ﷺ mean after Muhammad's name?
faq.answer: It is an Arabic blessing meaning that God's peace and blessings be upon him. Muslims say or write it as an expression of love and respect for the Prophet.

faq.question: Do Muslims worship Muhammad?
faq.answer: No. Muslims worship Allah alone. Muhammad is honored as God's servant, messenger, and final prophet, but assigning him divinity or directing worship to him would violate Tawhid.

faq.question: Did Muhammad write the Quran himself?
faq.answer: Islam's claim is that he received and recited revelation from God through Gabriel; he is its messenger, not its author. Historical study can examine the transmission and setting of that claim, while Muslim faith accepts the Quran as divine speech.

faq.question: How do Muslims know details of Muhammad's life?
faq.answer: The Quran provides the earliest scriptural setting, while biography and hadith literature preserve additional reports. Scholars assess those reports by studying transmission, wording, corroboration, chronology, and historical context rather than treating every later story as equally reliable.
